Signal restricts phone AI

20 November 2026 · Reading time: 4 minutes

Signal is restricting the AI agents built into iOS 27 and Android from capturing its chats. Meredith Whittaker calls the fix incomplete.

Sapaude retells the story in its own words. The source is below. Publisher: Sapaude.

In three points

Three points, in this order: what the source shows, where that claim stops, and what to check next.

  1. On November 20, Meredith Whittaker wrote on Signal's blog that the app now blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and turns on Screen security on Android when it detects an AI assistant reading the screen.
  2. Signal says the remedy is incomplete: it does not stop agents from reading data already on the device through the filesystem, it cannot cover every Android phone, and it does not work on macOS.
  3. According to Signal's support page, the option sits in Signal's privacy settings: Block Siri AI on iPhone (Signal 8.37 on iOS 27) and Screen security on Android (Signal 8.35.1).

Signal restricts AI agents on iOS and Android

Signal is restricting the AI agents built into mobile operating systems from capturing and storing Signal data. Meredith Whittaker announced the move on Signal's blog on November 20, 2026. She names Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI, features that scan the screen to answer questions and carry out tasks.

Signal has done this once before. Last year it used screenshot blocking on Windows 11 to keep Microsoft's Recall from storing Signal messages by default. Whittaker now calls the OS-level agents "an existential threat" to Signal. Once an agent has captured a chat, she writes, the data sits in whatever local database or remote server the agent uses, outside Signal's control, putting everyone in the conversation at risk.

Screenshots off on iPhone, detection on Android

On iOS 27, Signal now prevents screenshots inside the app. Android is harder. On many phones that don't run Google's Pixel software, Signal says it cannot reliably detect a screenshot attempt once screenshots are disabled. Instead it watches for an AI assistant trying to read the screen and then turns on Screen security automatically.

Signal's support page lists what the protection blocks: screenshots and screen recordings, chat previews in the recent-apps list or App Switcher, and on-device assistants reading the screen. Encryption and other settings are unchanged. On iPhone, Block Siri AI is on by default from Signal 8.37 on iOS 27. Besides On and Off, it offers "Off for 10 Minutes" for a quick screenshot. On Android, Screen security needs Signal 8.35.1 or later.

Files and Macs remain open

Whittaker calls the remedy incomplete. Blocking screenshots does not stop agents from reading content already stored on the device through the filesystem. Signal also cannot block Siri AI on macOS, because it says it has no reliable way to block screenshots there.

Her broader complaint is aimed at Apple, Google and Microsoft. Developers, she writes, have no easy, documented way to opt their apps out of AI data access without crippling the app. Signal is calling for exactly that, and for clear documentation of how these agents handle data. Whittaker says Google and Apple are engaging with Signal on the issue.

Check the setting and protect the Mac

People who want screenshots can switch the protection off. Signal warns that this may expose their own and their contacts' messages to these agents. According to the support page, the iPhone path is Settings → Privacy → Block Siri AI, and on Android it is Settings → Privacy → App security → Screen security, where it can be switched on before an assistant triggers it.

For macOS 27, Signal's only recommendation is to add Signal to Excluded Apps under System Settings → Siri.

What you can do

Update Signal and check the setting under Settings → Privacy. On a Mac with macOS 27, add Signal to Excluded Apps under System Settings → Siri, as Signal recommends.

In the app, the same story is also told shorter and in more detail, matched to your level.

Source: Signal. Published: 20 November 2026.
